newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says U.N. resolutions do not ban flights.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says U.N. resolutions do not ban flights.

text.p: United Nations resolutions do not bar Iraq from using its civilian planes for both domestic and international flights, a senior Foreign Ministry official was quoted on Wednesday as saying.

"There is absolutely no text in the (U.N.) Security Council resolutions referring to the existence of an air embargo from and to Iraq. There is no ban on flying passengers or air transport of humanitarian goods," Undersecretary Riyadh al-Qeisi said in remarks carried by the official Iraqi News Agency.
Qeisi said the United States was trying to link resolutions on sanctions imposed on Iraq for invading Kuwait in 1990 and the use of planes for civilian and humanitarian purposes.
But he said claims that the regime of sanctions included a ban on flights were "futile altogether".
He said several Security Council members supported Iraq's attitude and for this reason the United States failed to lobby the Council to condemn Iraq when it flew a pilgrim plane to Mecca last month.
Qeisi also said Iraq was trying to get U.N. permission to allow it to assemble its planes in Jordan for maintenance and repairs.

Iraq dispersed its fleet of 15 Boeing airliners to foreign airports to protect them against possible attack shortly before the 1991 Gulf War, in which a U.S.-led force ousted Iraqi forces from Kuwait.
Six of the Boeings are said to be in Amman and four in Tunis. A further five are in Tehran.
Qeisi said the United States and Britain rejected a demand by Baghdad to bring the planes back to Iraq.
Qeisi said Iraq would insist on the right to have its planes back to use them for domestic and international flights.
Iraq is under two no-fly zones -- one in the north and the other in the south -- enforced by U.S., British and French planes.
